Sends crash reports and anonymous usage statistics so problems can be found and fixed. Never your answers or your notes.
Has ClockOut helped you close your workday? A short rating on Google Play takes a minute and helps other people who struggle to switch off find the app.

ClockOut helps you consciously close your workday and switch from work into your own time. It matters most when you work from home, where the boundary between the office and the living room is missing.

All it takes is a three-minute daily ritual: answer today's question and park a thought you no longer need to carry, calm your breath at 4s in / 4s out, tap to turn off the desk lamp, and note the mood you are leaving the day with.

Work stops spilling into your evening, you unwind more easily, and you start the next day rested. Everything stays on your phone — no accounts, no cloud.

resources.string: The way home from work used to close the day by itself: shut the laptop, put on a coat, lock up, take the stairs and walk home. Working from home, that way is missing, and work easily spills into the evening.\n\nEvery day you close moves you a little further along a way you rebuild one day at a time. At the end of it you are home, which is where the evening belongs.

A week is in rhythm when you close all but one of its weekdays: four of five. With weekends on, a closed Saturday or Sunday counts as well and can stand in for a missed weekday. One weaker week will not break the rhythm, it just does not count; only two in a row do. The week you are in counts once it reaches the threshold.\n\nYour stage and your rhythm stay even when you clear the history. They remember only the dates you closed the day, nothing of what you wrote.
A new stage on the path
